newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI PHONE CO SEES FINNET DEAL HELPING IPO.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI PHONE CO SEES FINNET DEAL HELPING IPO.

text.p: Helsinki telephone company Helsingin Puhelin Oy on Wednesday welcomed a cooperation deal by regional telephone operators of the Finnet alliance and said it would facilitate its plans to issue shares.
"Managing director Kurt Nordman considered the proposed arrangement positive with a view to Helsingin Puhelin Oy's share issue plans," Helsingin Puhelin said in a statement.
Helsingin Puhelin Oy's owner Helsingin Puhelin Yhdistys (HPY) has said it plans to offer shares in the company this autumn, and that a listing is also on the agenda.
Fifteen percent or about 5.9 million shares of a total 40 million would be offered to domestic and international investors, an HPY official told Reuters in early February.
The company aims for a market capitalisation of "closer to four billion markka than three billion," the official said.
The current owners of HPY -- about 420,000 subscribers with some 550,000 mutal shares -- would all have subscription rights, but HPY has said it aims for a clearly smaller amount of shareholders.
The planned issue size would mean about 11 new shares per current mutual stake.
